issues.legal_issue: A court cannot refer a complaint for investigation against a public servant accused of a protected corruption offence without the required prior sanction.
material_facts: The complaint alleged that public officials had abused their official positions in connection with land-conversion proceedings.
The complaint was referred for investigation under the Code of Criminal Procedure before any sanction had been obtained.
issues.conclusion: A court cannot direct investigation under Section 156(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure against a public servant for an offence covered by Section 19 of the Prevention of Corruption Act in the absence of valid prior sanction.
issues.legal_principle: Section 19(1) of the Prevention of Corruption Act bars a court from taking cognizance of the specified offences against a public servant without prior sanction. Applying the broad meaning of cognizance, the court held that a judicial referral for investigation under Section 156(3) also requires sanction. It relied on Anil Kumar v. M.K. Aiyappa, which directly held that sanction is required before such a referral, and on Manharibhai Muljibhai Kakadia v. Shaileshbhai Mohanbhai Patel, which explained that cognizance includes taking authoritative notice of allegations through application of judicial mind. It also referred to Section 190 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the principles in State of U.P. v. Paras Nath Singh and Subramanian Swamy v. Manmohan Singh.

predicates.magistrate_refers_complaint_for_investig: A magistrate refers a complaint for investigation before taking cognizance of the alleged offence.
predicates.public_servant_is_accused_of_protected_c: The complaint accuses a public servant of an offence for which the law requires prior sanction before the court may take cognizance.
predicates.valid_prior_sanction_obtained: The authority competent to grant sanction has given valid prior approval for the prosecution.

issues.definition: When a magistrate refers a complaint for investigation into a protected corruption offence allegedly committed by a public servant, the referral is not permissible if valid prior sanction has not been obtained.

issues.legal_issue: Prior sanction is not required when, at the time cognizance is taken, the public servant no longer holds the office alleged to have been abused, even if the person remains a public servant in another office.
material_facts: The alleged misconduct related to offices the appellants had held earlier.
By the time cognizance was taken, the appellants had been transferred or promoted and no longer held the offices alleged to have been abused.
The appellants remained public servants in different posts.
issues.conclusion: Sanction was not required in this case because, when cognizance was taken, the appellants did not hold the posts alleged to have been misused.
issues.legal_principle: Section 19(1) of the Prevention of Corruption Act requires sanction by reference to the office alleged to have been abused and the public servant's position when cognizance is taken. If the public servant has ceased to hold that office, or holds a different office, sanction is not required merely because the person remains a public servant. The court relied on Abhay Singh Chautala v. Central Bureau of Investigation, S.A. Venkataraman v. State, and Prakash Singh Badal v. State of Punjab, and referred to R.S. Nayak v. A.R. Antulay for the connection between an alleged abuse and the office that enabled it. The principle applies to public servants generally, including government employees.

predicates.corruption_prosecution_requires_sanction: The prosecution concerns an offence for which the law would require sanction if the accused still held the office alleged to have been abused.
predicates.cognizance_is_taken: A court takes cognizance of the alleged offence against the public servant.
predicates.alleged_office_abuse_occurred_in_differe: The alleged corrupt conduct is attributed to an office different from the office the public servant holds when cognizance is taken.
predicates.public_servant_does_not_hold_alleged_off: When cognizance is taken, the accused has ceased to hold the office alleged to have been abused, whether or not the accused remains a public servant in another role.

issues.definition: If a corruption prosecution concerns alleged abuse of an office that the public servant no longer holds when cognizance is taken, prior sanction is not required on that basis.

issues.legal_issue: A prosecution should not be quashed at the threshold when the complaint attributes specific official acts to public officials and their asserted innocent explanation depends on disputed facts requiring evidence.
material_facts: The complaint alleged that officials recommended a land conversion and issued an endorsement stating that the land was not subject to acquisition.
The complaint alleged that the officials acted despite circumstances involving competing claims to the land and land that had already been acquired.
The appellants argued that they had merely acted on a court decree, but the court considered whether they had failed to account for the competing claims and acquisition as matters for evidence.
issues.conclusion: The allegations against the appellants were sufficient to prevent quashing at this stage; their explanation and culpability were matters to be assessed on evidence.
issues.legal_principle: At the threshold, proceedings should not be quashed on the basis of an asserted defence when the complaint attributes official acts to the accused and alleges circumstances that could indicate abuse of office. Whether the officials acted innocently or culpably depends on the evidence. The court relied on the allegations in the complaint and treated the appellants' explanation as a matter for trial rather than accepting it as a basis for quashing.

predicates.threshold_quashing_challenge: An accused person asks a court to terminate criminal proceedings before the allegations have been tested at trial.
predicates.complaint_attributes_official_acts_to_ac: The complaint identifies official acts performed by the accused and alleges that those acts assisted the alleged wrongdoing.
predicates.alleged_irregularities_require_evidence: The complaint alleges circumstances suggesting that the official acts may have disregarded material competing claims or other relevant facts.
predicates.asserted_defence_depends_on_disputed_fac: The accused's explanation depends on facts whose truth or significance must be assessed through evidence.

issues.definition: When a threshold challenge concerns specific alleged official acts and the accused's explanation depends on disputed facts requiring evidence, the proceeding is not quashed at that stage.
